html:
Bosnia-Herzegovina was an Ottoman province in the western Balkans that Austria-Hungary occupied in 1878 and ruled until 1918. It is shown here in 1880 and 1900.

A peasant revolt in Herzegovina in 1875 set off a Balkan crisis and a war between Russia and the Ottomans. The Congress of Berlin in 1878 let Austria-Hungary occupy and run the province, while the sultan kept the title. Habsburg rule built railways, schools and offices in Sarajevo, but most land stayed with Muslim landlords, worked by Christian peasants.

The population was mixed: Muslim Bosniaks, Orthodox Serbs and Catholic Croats. In 1908 Austria-Hungary annexed it outright, which caused the Bosnian crisis and angered Serbia. In 1914 a young Bosnian Serb shot the heir to the throne in Sarajevo, the assassination that started the First World War. In 1918 the province joined the new kingdom that became Yugoslavia.
